chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: Fletcher Henderson's band at Roseland
summary: The Goldkette and Henderson bands alternated at Roseland, with Redman, Buster Bailey and Hawkins, and musicians filled the hall.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I don't know if you read Jazz Masters of the Thirties by Rex Stewart, but he had a whole chapter in there on the Goldkette band.
Well, Don Redman was there, saxophone.
Let's see I think he was their lead and you know, the one and only clarinet player, I liked him, tall, thin fellow.
Buster Bailey and there was the tenor sax, Hawkins. Oh, they had a great band. Really a fine band.
Were they there when you came to Roseland, like the overlapping.
So you come to New York and that's the first thing you hear.

That's the first thing you hear and besides most of the guys that come up there to listen were musicians. They filled up Roseland and they gave them a lot of enthusiastic support too. And besides to hear both bands --
That would be the thing, if you know that both bands are going to be there on one night, the same night, you're going to go and hear it.
